note: Embeds a chunk of HTML (or xhtml / mht / rtf / plain text) into the document using Word's native alternative-format import: the payload is stored verbatim in its own package part (word/afchunkN.htm) and referenced from the body by <w:altChunk r:id="…"/>. Word converts the chunk into native paragraphs, tables, lists and images when the document is opened — full HTML/CSS fidelity without OfficeCLI translating the markup (contrast 'markdown', which expands into native elements immediately). Add returns /body/altChunk[N]. Until Word has opened and re-saved the file the chunk stays a single altChunk node: 'get' shows it, 'view html' / preview render its source as escaped text (never as live HTML), and its content is not searchable/editable via paragraph paths. An HTML fragment (no <html>/<!DOCTYPE>) is wrapped in a minimal UTF-8 document; a complete HTML document is stored as-is. Only the main document body and its table cells are supported (not headers, footers, footnotes). Round-trips through dump→batch as 'add htmlchunk'. KNOWN LIMITATIONS: rendering depends on the consuming application — Word imports altChunk; LibreOffice imports HTML chunks; Google Docs and some viewers ignore them. Relative image/link URLs inside the HTML are not resolved; use absolute http(s) URLs or data: URIs. Headless conversion without Word: `officecli materialize file.docx` replaces HTML/XHTML/plain-text altChunks with native paragraphs, lists, tables and links (a subset — images are not embedded, RTF/MHT stay as altChunks; see `officecli materialize --help`).

html.description:
HTML markup to embed — a fragment ('

Title

…
') or a complete document. Aliases: content, text. Takes precedence over src.

src.description: Path to a file to embed (used when no inline html/content/text is given). The format is inferred from the extension: .html/.htm → html, .xhtml → xhtml, .mht/.mhtml → mht, .rtf → rtf, .txt → text; anything else is treated as html. Complete documents are stored byte-for-byte (their own charset applies). Alias: path.

format.description: Payload format (sets the chunk part's content type). Default: inferred from the src extension, else html.

matchSrc.description: Writes <w:altChunkPr><w:matchSrc/></w:altChunkPr>: ask Word to keep the chunk's source formatting instead of adapting it to the destination document's styles.

title.description: Optional <title> for the wrapper document generated around an HTML fragment. Ignored for complete documents and non-HTML formats.
